title: At least one argument
hints: A required first parameter followed by ...int makes "no arguments at all" a compile error, so Max never has to handle an empty call.
Start the running maximum at first, not at 0, or negative inputs break. In JoinNonEmpty, skip empty strings before adding a separator.
Max: best := first; for _, n := range rest { best = max(best, n) }. JoinNonEmpty: collect the non-empty parts into a slice, then return strings.Join(kept, sep).
